messages.subject: Stan v2.0.2 up next
parts:
I want to get a patch release out to fix the bugs that
are outstanding in 2.0.1.

All work for 2.0.2 should be in branches from this branch:

hotfix/v2.0.2

I updated our developer process doc to reflect the new
process --- we're still trying to get right with the Git
process and messed up this time by just branching the hotfix/v2.0.2
branch from develop today rather than branching it from master
when v2.0.1 was released.

Work can continue on develop, but it's not going into the
next release.

If you have bug fix branches from develop, we need to get
Ben's input on how to proceed --- neither Daniel nor I know how
to deal with that case.

Given the slowness of our unit tests and merging and the fact
that Daniel's still rebuilding Jenkins, v2.0.2 won't happen for
a week or two.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stan v2.0.2 up next
parts:
The intent of gitflow is basically that a critical bugfix goes into a hotfix branch (and gets merged into develop) while noncritical bugs are fixed in develop only. Basically, hotfix branches have approximately one commit and there is a new release as soon as it is verified that the patch actually fixes the bug.

I think that is fine in general. I was just saying that if you have already branched from develop (whether that was appropriate in retrospect or not), it is probably better to make a normal release from that branch, as opposed to trying to cherry-pick parts of it onto a branch off master.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Stan v2.0.2 up next
parts:
I think that most people who use gitflow would not really accept the idea of doing a bugfix release whenever you want; rather you do a bugfix release whenever you have to. If none of the bugs rise to that level of severity, then I think it is fine to push the fixes into develop and then do a normal release whenever you want. The problem we had with 2.0 was that we couldn't do a normal release when we wanted to because a lot of big but interrelated stuff was being merged intermittently.

But if develop is in good shape now, then I don't think there is really anything wrong with treating the "hotfix" branch you made as a "release" branch.

Ben

>      >      >     a week or two.

>      >      >     - Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan v2.0.2 up next
parts:
In other words, you only create a hotfix branch when you don't want to include all of
develop in the new version, just the new fix. If you don't use the hotfix procedure in
gitflow then, as Ben noted, you have to cherry pick through all of the updates to the
develop branch to create the release candidate.

On Nov 14, 2013, at 5:48 AM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I think that most people who use gitflow would not really accept the idea of doing a bugfix release whenever you want; rather you do a bugfix release whenever you have to. If none of the bugs rise to that level of severity, then I think it is fine to push the fixes into develop and then do a normal release whenever you want. The problem we had with 2.0 was that we couldn't do a normal release when we wanted to because a lot of big but interrelated stuff was being merged intermittently.
>
> But if develop is in good shape now, then I don't think there is really anything wrong with treating the "hotfix" branch you made as a "release" branch.
>
> Ben
>
> On Wednesday, November 13, 2013 9:27:12 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> We blew it today in naming convention and (maybe?) in concept.
>
> If I understand what Ben wrote below, we'll probably never
> need a hotfix branch.
>
> Should we have created a 2.0.2 release branch instead?
> And then all new work on bug fixes for 2.0.2 goes there?
>
> I'm still having a hard time converting the high-level
> desiderata into git commands.
>
> So what do we do if after a release, we want to
> triage code into:
>
> (a) bug fixes
>
> (b) new features
>
> so that we can roll out a bug fix release whenever
> we want.
>
> Or is this just a bad idea?
>
> I really want to stabilized because the process already has me
> deeply confused whenever I try to work on code. I'm really slow
> with all of this moving things around.
>
> - Bob
>
>
> On 11/13/13, 9:11 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> > The intent of gitflow is basically that a critical bugfix goes into a hotfix branch (and gets merged into develop) while
> > noncritical bugs are fixed in develop only. Basically, hotfix branches have approximately one commit and there is a new
> > release as soon as it is verified that the patch actually fixes the bug.
> >
> > I think that is fine in general. I was just saying that if you have already branched from develop (whether that was
> > appropriate in retrospect or not), it is probably better to make a normal release from that branch, as opposed to trying
> > to cherry-pick parts of it onto a branch off master.
> >
> > Ben
> >
> > On Wednesday, November 13, 2013 8:29:03 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> >
> > I would like to release a 2.0.2 version which consists
> > of what we have in develop up to now plus some
> > more bug fixes.
> >
> > Ben --- can you work out with Daniel how to organize
> > this in GitHub so that you (Ben) are happy with it?
> > I don't care what the process is as long as
> >
> > (a) it doesn't keep changing, and
> >
> > (b) there are instructions in the Developer Process
> > Wiki that I can follow to create a branch to
> > work on for either bug fixes or new features.
> >
> > - Bob
> >
> > On 11/13/13, 8:16 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> > > If you already branched from develop, then it is probably easiest to just make this a "normal" release with very
> > few if
> > > any new features. Is there anything that got into develop recently that is manifestly not ready to release? (If
> > so, that
> > > is another workflow problem).
> > >
> > > Ben
> > >
> > > On Wednesday, November 13, 2013 7:31:15 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> > >
> > > We did branch from develop and this is intended
> > > to be for the 2.0.2 release. Should the branch
> > > have a different name?
> > >
> > > The plan going forward is to immediately branch
> > > a hotfix branch from master after a release and
> > > put bug fixes there and new features on develop.
> > >
> > > - Bob
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On 11/13/13, 7:22 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> > > > How many bugfix branches are we talking about here? Maybe we can cherry-pick merges or maybe we should
> > just branch a
> > > > release from develop.
> > > >
> > > > Ben
> > > >
> > > > On Wednesday, November 13, 2013 4:10:10 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> > > >
> > > > I want to get a patch release out to fix the bugs that
> > > > are outstanding in 2.0.1.
> > > >
> > > > All work for 2.0.2 should be in branches from this branch:
> > > >
> > > > hotfix/v2.0.2
> > > >
> > > > I updated our developer process doc to reflect the new
> > > > process --- we're still trying to get right with the Git
> > > > process and messed up this time by just branching the hotfix/v2.0.2
> > > > branch from develop today rather than branching it from master
> > > > when v2.0.1 was released.
> > > >
> > > > Work can continue on develop, but it's not going into the
> > > > next release.
> > > >
> > > > If you have bug fix branches from develop, we need to get
> > > > Ben's input on how to proceed --- neither Daniel nor I know how
> > > > to deal with that case.
> > > >
> > > > Given the slowness of our unit tests and merging and the fact
> > > > that Daniel's still rebuilding Jenkins, v2.0.2 won't happen for
> > > > a week or two.
> > > >
> > > > - Bob
